Which of the following reactions are used in the preparation of aliphatic primary amines?
I. Gabriel-phthalimide reaction
II. Hoffmann Bromamide reaction
III. Carbylamine reaction
IV. Sandmayer reaction
questions.solution:
Gabriel-phthalimide and Hoffmann- bromamide reactions are used for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines.
Carbylamine reaction or isocyanide test is used to check the presence of a primary amine that gives a bad-smelling isocyanide.
Sandmeyer reaction is also a reaction of amines that converts an amine to halobenzene.
Thus, only I and II give a primary aliphatic amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $NaCl$ is a $FCC$ lattice where ${Na}^{+}$ ions are at corner and face centre positions. Chloride ions are at edge centres and body centre positions. How many $NaCl$ formula units will be in an unit cell
questions.solution:
Here, it is given that& $NaCl$ is a& $FCC$ lattice.

& ${Na}^{+}$ ions occupy corner positions and face centres of the cube and& ${Cl}^{-}$ ions are& located at the centre of the cube.

We know that,

There are& $8$ corners present in a cube and each corner contributes& $\dfrac{1}{8}th$ to the unit cell& and& $6$ faces& present in a cube and each face centre& contributes& $\dfrac{1}{2}th$ to the unit cell.

Number of ${Na}^{+}$ ions corners and face centres =& $1 + 3 = 4$

And for ${Cl}^{-}$,

There are $12$ edge centres in a cube and each contributes& $\dfrac{1}{4}th$ to the unit cell and there is& $1$ body centre present in a cube which fully contributes to unit cell.

Number of& ${Cl}^{-}$ ions& edge centres& and body centre& =& $3 + 1 = 4$

Hence, units of $NaCl = 4$
